plain: monodromy, the owner's maths library, is written in Python 3.11+ under the MIT license, not in Rust.
monodromy needs numpy, scipy, ripser, persim and mpmath to run; pytest and scikit-learn only for its tests.
phdim.py offers total_persistence, ph_dimension, is_fractal and TOPOLOGICAL_DIM, and uses the ripser library to compute persistence.

dynamics.py offers henon, holmes, sample_attractor, attractor_sampler, jacobians_along, map_spectrum, equivariance_defect, trust_horizon and kaplan_yorke_dimension; it has no Lorenz function (that lives in thesis.py).
equilibrium.py offers error_rates, minimax_threshold, game_value, relative_margin and equalizer_gap.
schedule.py offers Budget, bonferroni, coarse_to_fine and successive_halving; unit_cost exists but is not exported.
injectivity.py offers twelve public names, from local_floor to certified_injectivity_radius; free_ratio_is_readable exists but is not exported.
monodromy's own docs say two of its slope measurements (lambda_n and m(R)) have no theorem behind them, unlike its Lyapunov and PH-dimension estimates.
monodromy's docs say its threshold game is a two-player zero-sum minimax, not a Nash equilibrium of a general game.
These monodromy facts were read at commit 2e5f7d0 (12 October 2026).
In Minecraft the same seed always builds the same terrain, but only on the same game version: a new version can turn the same seed into a different world.
Java and Bedrock Minecraft share terrain and biomes for a seed, but structures, decorations, caves and mob spawns differ.
speedrun.com lists Minecraft Any%, Any% Glitchless, and Random Seed and Set Seed categories (with and without glitches), among 13 in total.
Any% Glitchless runs are split by seed type (random or set) and by version range (Pre 1.8, 1.8, 1.9-1.12, 1.13-1.15, 1.16-1.19, 1.20+).
A typical random-seed run goes: Nether portal, bastion (pearls from piglins), fortress (blaze rods), eyes of ender, stronghold, End, kill the dragon.
1.16-1.19 Minecraft speedruns are mostly played on version 1.16.1.
cubiomes, a free C library (MIT), copies Minecraft Java's biome and structure placement from a seed, but not the individual blocks.
Amidst (Java, GPL-3.0) and the SeedFinding Java libraries (MIT) also reproduce parts of Minecraft world generation.
Crafter worlds are 64 by 64 tiles, the agent sees a 9 by 9 window, and an episode lasts at most 10,000 steps.
Crafter makes each episode's world from a hash of the seed and the episode number, then grows terrain with simplex noise.
Crafter has 22 achievements, from collecting wood to collecting a diamond.
The standard persistent homology algorithm can take cubic time (N^3 steps for N cells) in the worst case.
The fastest known zigzag persistence runs in matrix-multiplication time, about n^2.376, versus the old n^3.
Counting connected pieces with union-find costs almost constant time per step (inverse Ackermann), and that is provably optimal.
Keeping track of connected pieces while edges are also removed costs O(log^2 n) per change with the Holm-de Lichtenberg-Thorup method.
source: Holm, de Lichtenberg, Thorup, J. ACM 48:723-760, 2001

plain: No method can track connectivity under insertions and deletions faster than about log n per change (cell-probe lower bound).
For a flat grid of squares, corners minus edges plus faces equals islands minus loops plus enclosed voids (b0 - b1 + b2).
